readBy: the video-readiness lane, 2026-09-07, from contact sheets built by video_event_ledger.py
method: Every 8th frame of each view, selected BY INDEX from the container's pts list and never by seeking, tiled into contact sheets and read by eye. An event's time is therefore the sampled frame nearest it, so each is accurate to about one sample, 0.267 s. THAT IS COARSE ON PURPOSE AND IT IS ENOUGH: the question is whether ONE constant offset maps one view's sequence onto the other's, and the disagreement below is many times the resolution. If a fit had been found at this resolution it would then have needed refining to frame-exactness.

front.note: Hands EMPTY at her hips from 0.0 to 8.5 s, then a first catch of a ball arriving from off-frame. A second empty stretch runs 17.3 to 20.0 s and holds the second clap. The camera is picked up at 26.1 s and the frame goes dark.
front.readingStepNote: READ AT EVERY EIGHTH FRAME, except the first catch at index 274, which was refined frame by frame when pair 1 was pinned. Nine of the ten indices are multiples of 8; 274 is not, and that is the refined one.

side.note: A first catch at 8.26 of a ball fed from the front camera's side, held, then RELEASED UPWARD at 8.53 and caught again at 9.86. SHE IS NOT HANDLING A BALL WITHOUT PAUSE THROUGH 17.06-19.73 — an earlier version of this note said so and the contact sheet refutes it: she releases at about 17.5 and her hands are empty from 17.59 to 18.39 before catching at 18.53. What survives, and what matters, is that NO EMPTY STRETCH IN THIS VIEW AFTER 8.26 s LASTS MUCH OVER A SECOND, while the front stands empty for 2.7 s. She walks off at 26.4 s.
side.readingStepNote:
READ AT EVERY EIGHTH FRAME, and that was not recorded until 2026-09-07. Every index here is a multiple of 8. A time sampled every eighth frame is not a measurement of when something happened, and a fit that consumes it as one gets a confident wrong answer: this ledger produced a NO FIT for `front 0.2.mp4` against this very file, which is a real pair at -78.

AND THE ERROR IS NOT BOUNDED BY THE STEP. The four rows re-read frame by frame are late by 2, 10, 3 and 13 frames. The step explains at most 8. The reader recorded the frame where the ball was clearly HELD rather than the frame it met the hands, and sometimes took the sample after that, so `framesLate` is a measured quantity here and not a bound.

`usable_for_a_fit` in video_event_ledger.py now refuses every row of this ledger at a one-frame tolerance, and says why.

fit.why: a sync needs two anchors at least 10.0 s apart and the best offset spans 5.333 s; a RANDOM side ledger of the same shape explains 4 events at the 99th percentile, so 3 is not better than chance

verdict: NOT A SYNCHRONOUS PAIR — AND NOW EXPLAINED
why:
THE TWO FILES THIS LEDGER COMPARED ARE NOT A PAIR, and the reason is not a discontinuity or a drop: THE FILE NAMES WERE WRONG, AND MARIUS CORRECTED THEM AT SOURCE ON 2026-09-07. This ledger read `front 0.1.mp4` (f7faf38b5d42) against 253fa551605e, which was called `side 0.1.mp4` then and is called `side 0.2.mp4` now. `front 0.1.mp4` pairs instead with 6e8f9fb2fe03, called `side 0.2.mp4` then and `side 0.1.mp4` now, at a constant frame offset of -5, established on two ball-into-hands anchors 11.03 s apart and checked on a third event. That is why no offset fits the labelled pair at any tolerance a sync could use: at one frame the best explains 3 of 10 events against a chance ceiling of 4.

THE SEQUENCE SAID SO BEFORE THE ARITHMETIC DID. The front stands empty-handed from 17.3 to 20.0 s and claps at 17.87, and `side 0.1.mp4` has no comparable gap: its longest empty stretch after 8.26 s is about 0.8 s, from 17.59 to 18.39. (This sentence used to say the side handles a ball CONTINUOUSLY through 17.06-19.73; the contact sheet refutes that and the note on the side view says so. The conclusion is unchanged and now rests on the durations.) No offset reconciles a 2.7 s pause with a view whose gaps are all about a second — and `side 0.2.mp4` DOES contain that pause, at 17.33 to 19.73, which is what identified it.

Refer to PAIRS in spikes/video_keypoints.py.
resolutionNote: Events are read on a grid of every eighth frame, so their times are multiples of 8 frames — EXCEPT the front's first catch at index 274, which is not. That one was pinned to its contact frame afterwards, when it became an anchor, and it is left at its true index rather than pushed back onto the grid: an anchor's value is that it is exact. The other rows are grid samples and are accurate to about one sample, 0.267 s.
identityNote: THE FILE NAMES IN THIS LEDGER'S OWN NAME ARE PRE-RENAME. This file is called `event-ledger-0.1.json`, and it was made when the two side files' names were the other way round. Each view now carries the file it actually read, by NAME AND BY sha256, and the hash is the identity. Read `videoSha256`, never the ledger's file name and never the view's set id. On 2026-09-07 Marius swapped the two side names at source; no content and no event time changed.
